Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and defining ideal of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and write $K_i=K_{d_i h_i}$. Let $\Delta:T\to T\otimes_{\mathbb Q(q)}T$ and $\varepsilon:T\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the algebra homomorphisms determined by

$$\Delta(K_h)=K_h\otimes K_h,\quad \Delta(E_i)=E_i\otimes K_i^{-1}+1\otimes E_i,\quad \Delta(F_i)=F_i\otimes1+K_i\otimes F_i,\quad \varepsilon(K_h)=1,\quad\varepsilon(E_i)=\varepsilon(F_i)=0.$$

Let $S:T\to T$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear algebra anti-homomorphism determined by

$$S(K_h)=K_{-h},\qquad S(E_i)=-E_iK_i,\qquad S(F_i)=-K_i^{-1}F_i.$$

Then

$$\Delta(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}\otimes T+T\otimes I_{\mathrm{DJ}},\qquad \varepsilon(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})=0,\qquad S(I_{\mathrm{DJ}})\subseteq I_{\mathrm{DJ}}.$$

Hence these maps descend to $U_q(\mathfrak g)=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and make it a Hopf algebra over $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[def-bialgebra-counit-and-antipode]]): $\Delta$ is coassociative, $\varepsilon$ is a counit, and

$$m(S\otimes\operatorname{id})\Delta=\eta\circ\varepsilon=m(\operatorname{id}\otimes S)\Delta.$$

The antipode $S$ is unique for this multiplication, unit, coproduct and counit ([[lem-an-antipode-is-unique]]), and its square satisfies

$$S^2(E_i)=q_i^{-2}E_i,\qquad S^2(F_i)=q_i^{2}F_i,\qquad S^2(K_h)=K_h.$$

Let $\psi$ (the bar involution) and $\tau$ (the contravariant anti-involution) be
the semilinear maps of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]], so
that $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(F_i)=F_i$, $\psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$
and $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$, $\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1}$,
with $\tau$ anti-multiplicative. Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$ be
the Lusztig divided-power integral form with its generators $E_i^{(r)}$,
$F_i^{(r)}$, $K_h^{\pm1}$ and toral binomials $T_{i,c,t}$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then $\psi(U_A)=U_A$ and
$\tau(U_A)=U_A$. Explicitly, on the generators,

$$\psi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \psi(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \psi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t},$$

$$\tau(E_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(F_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)},\quad \tau(K_h)=K_h^{-1},\quad \tau(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}.$$

In particular both maps restrict to bijections of $U_A$: $\psi$ to a semilinear
algebra involution of $U_A$ and $\tau$ to a semilinear anti-involution of
$U_A$, while $q^{\pm1}\in A$ keeps all coefficients in $A$. These are the two
involutions under which the bar lattice and the contravariant duality of the
later constructions are taken; neither formula is the Chevalley involution
$\omega$, which changes signs, exchanges the two halves and is treated in
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
No choice is used.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S=\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

derivations.claim: **The parameter transport respects every defining relation.** Apply the assignment $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i^L\mapsto E_i$, $F_i^L\mapsto F_i$, $K_h^L\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ to the source relations. The toral relations become $K_h^{-1}K_{h'}^{-1}=K_{h+h'}^{-1}$ and $K_0^{-1}=1$, which are the library toral relations. For the toral action, $v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}=(q^{-1})^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$ and the library relation $K_h^{-1}E_i=q^{\langle\alpha_i,-h\rangle}E_iK_h^{-1}=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h^{-1}$ is exactly the image; the $F$-relation is the same computation with the sign of the exponent reversed. The mixed relation maps to $E_iF_j-F_jE_i=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{-1}-K_i)/(q_i^{-1}-q_i)=\delta_{ij}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, because numerator and denominator both change sign. In the Serre relations the coefficients are $v_i$-Gaussian binomials, the generators map to $E_i$ or $F_i$, and $[m]_{v_i}=(v_i^m-v_i^{-m})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})=(q_i^{-m}-q_i^{m})/(q_i^{-1}-q_i)=[m]_{q_i}$ together with the symmetry $\binom{m}{r}_i=\binom{m}{m-r}_i$ makes each Serre polynomial identical term by term to the library one; the inverse assignment $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_h^{-1}$ reverses the transport.

**The transport is an involutive semilinear automorphism fixing the integral form.** By [F1] the assignment of step 1.1 extends uniquely to a semilinear algebra homomorphism $\varphi:U_q(\mathfrak g)\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$, since the image of each defining relation is a defining relation; the same universal property applies to the inverse assignment, so $\varphi$ is a bijection, and $\varphi\circ\varphi=\operatorname{id}$ because both sides are semilinear algebra maps agreeing on the generators. On generators $\varphi$ agrees with the bar involution $\psi$ of [F3], so $\varphi=\psi$; hence $\varphi$ preserves $A$ coefficients, inverts each $K_h$, and fixes each divided power $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)}$ and each toral binomial $T_{i,c,t}$, so $\varphi(U_A)=U_A$ with the stated generator values.

**The abstract half and the twisted product.** Under the transport $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ one has $\theta_i^{(n)}\mapsto\theta_i^n/[n]_{v_i}!=F_i^n/[n]_{q_i}!=F_i^{(n)}$, since $[n]_{v_i}=[n]_{q_i}$ by step 1.1; the half is generated by the $\theta_i$ with the source Serre relations, and those map to the $F_i$-Serre relations of [F1], so the transported half is $U_q^-$ and the divided powers match. The source twisted multiplication carries the coefficient $v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}$; under $v=q^{-1}$ and the degree sign reversal $\deg\theta_i=\alpha_i\mapsto\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ this coefficient becomes $q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}$ in the transported degrees, which is the displayed formula. Extracting from the transported twisted coproduct the coefficient of $\theta_i\otimes(\text{remaining word})$, i.e. of $F_i\otimes\cdot$, yields $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$: this is exactly the twisted Leibniz rule of [F5] evaluated on $F_j$, since $\langle\operatorname{wt}F_j,h_i\rangle=-a_{ij}$, and the recursion determines the extracted coefficient map uniquely from $e_i'(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$.

**Coproduct transport.** The source coproduct $\Delta_L$ and the library coproducts are algebra homomorphisms, so it suffices to compare them on generators. One computes $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\Delta_L(K_h^L)=K_h^{-1}\otimes K_h^{-1}=\Delta(K_h^{-1})=\Delta(\varphi K_h^L)$; $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\Delta_L(E_i^L)=E_i\otimes1+K_i^{-1}\otimes E_i=K_i^{-1}\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes1=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(E_i)=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(\varphi E_i^L)$; and $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\Delta_L(F_i^L)=F_i\otimes K_i+1\otimes F_i=1\otimes F_i+F_i\otimes K_i=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(F_i)=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(\varphi F_i^L)$, using $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(E_i)=K_i^{-1}\otimes E_i+E_i\otimes1$ and $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}(F_i)=1\otimes F_i+F_i\otimes K_i$ from [F2]. Both sides are semilinear algebra homomorphisms out of the source presentation, so $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$ holds on all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$; equivalently $\Delta\circ\varphi=\mathrm{flip}\circ(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L$, so the flip of the transported source coproduct is the library coproduct $\Delta$. Defining $\bar\Delta(u)=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$ and using $\varphi=\psi$, the transport of the intertwining convention follows: applying $\varphi\otimes\varphi$ and flip to the source identity for $\Delta_L$ produces an element $\Theta$ of the completed tensor square satisfying $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$, because after transport $\bar\Delta=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta_L$ on generators.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

The two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

derivations.claim: **The kernel and the two chart products.** Because $M$ is an $A$-module, $qM\subseteq M$ and $q^{-1}M\subseteq M$; hence $M\cap qL_0=q(M\cap L_0)$ and $M\cap q^{-1}L_\infty=q^{-1}(M\cap L_\infty)$. If the canonical map $E\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ of (1) is injective, its kernel is $E\cap qL_0=E\cap M\cap qL_0$, so $E\cap qL_0=0$.

**Peeling at the zero chart.** Assume from here through the end of part (1) that the canonical map $E\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ in (1) is an isomorphism. Surjectivity says that every $x\in M\cap L_0$ has the form $x=e+qx_1$ with $e\in E$ and $x_1\in M\cap L_0$; iterating gives $M\cap L_0\subseteq\sum_{k=0}^nq^kE+M\cap q^{n+1}L_0$ for every $n\ge0$.

**The overlap of a chart with the opposite vanishing order.** For $v\in M\cap qL_0\cap L_\infty$ write $v=qw$ with $w\in M\cap L_0$; then $w=q^{-1}v\in q^{-1}L_\infty\subseteq L_\infty$, so $w\in M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty=E$ and $v\in qE$. Conversely $qE\subseteq M\cap qL_0\cap L_\infty$ because $E\subseteq L_0\cap L_\infty$ and $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]L_\infty$-charts are $q$-stable. Hence $M\cap qL_0\cap L_\infty=qE$.

**Bounded infinity-pole pieces.** Intersecting the inclusion of step 2.1 with $q^nL_\infty$ gives $M\cap L_0\cap q^nL_\infty\subseteq\sum_{k=0}^nq^kE+q^n(M\cap qL_0\cap L_\infty)=\sum_{k=0}^nq^kE+q^{n+1}E=\sum_{k=0}^nq^kE$, using step 2.2 and $q^{n+1}E\subseteq q^nE$; the reverse inclusion holds because $q^kE\subseteq q^nL_\infty$ for $k\le n$ and $E\subseteq L_\infty$. Therefore $M\cap L_0\cap q^nL_\infty=\sum_{k=0}^nq^kE$ for every $n\ge0$.

**Identification of the zero-chart module.** Every $x\in M\cap L_0\subseteq V$ lies in $q^nL_\infty$ for some $n\ge0$, because $L_\infty$ spans $V$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ and $x=q^{-n}y$ has bounded infinity-pole order; combined with step 3.1 this gives $M\cap L_0=\sum_{k\ge0}q^kE=\mathbb Z[q]E$. The sum is direct: if $\sum_{k=0}^nq^ke_k=0$ with $e_k\in E$, then $e_0\in qL_0\cap E=0$ by step 1.1, and dividing by $q$ and repeating removes the remaining coefficients. Hence the inclusion $\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to M\cap L_0$ is an isomorphism.

**The Laurent module and the field of fractions.** Let $x\in M$. Since $M\cap L_0$ spans $V$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$ and $M$ is an $A$-module, $x$ can be written as a finite sum $\sum_kc_ky_k$ with $c_k\in A$ and $y_k\in M\cap L_0$: clearing the zero-chart poles of a $\mathbb Q(q)$-combination of $M\cap L_0$-vectors multiplies by a power of $q$, which stays inside $A$ and inside $M$. Thus $M=A(M\cap L_0)=A\otimes_ZE$ by step 4.1, and taking $\mathbb Q(q)$-spans gives $V=\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E$.

**The chart lattices.** The quotient $L_0/(M\cap L_0)$ is a finitely generated torsion $A_0$-module: $L_0$ is finitely generated over the noetherian local ring $A_0$, and each generator is killed by some power of $q$ because $M\cap L_0$ spans $V$. Hence $L_0=(M\cap L_0)+qL_0$, and Nakayama's lemma for the finitely generated $A_0$-module $L_0/A_0(M\cap L_0)$ gives $L_0=A_0(M\cap L_0)=A_0E$, so the induced map $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\to L_0$ is an isomorphism; the same argument with $q^{-1}$ in place of $q$ is used for the opposite chart.

**The infinity chart and the mirror residue.** The vanishing $E\cap qL_0=0$ of step 1.1 dualizes to $E\cap q^{-1}L_\infty=0$: if $e\in E$ and $e=q^{-1}v$ with $v\in M\cap L_\infty$, then $v=qe\in M\cap qL_0\cap L_\infty=qE$ by step 2.2, so $v=qf$ with $f\in E$ and then $e=f$ has $e\in E\cap qL_0=0$. Similarly, using the expansion $M=A E=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]E$ of step 5.1, every $x\in M\cap L_\infty$ satisfies $x\equiv e\pmod{q^{-1}(M\cap L_\infty)}$ for some $e\in E$: terms of the Laurent expansion with exponent $\ge1$ lie in $q(M\cap L_\infty)\subseteq q^{-1}(M\cap L_\infty)$, and terms with exponent $\le-1$ lie in $q^{-1}(M\cap L_\infty)$ because $q^{-1}L_\infty\subseteq L_\infty$. Running the peeling argument of steps 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 with $(q,L_0)$ replaced by $(q^{-1},L_\infty)$ therefore yields $M\cap L_\infty=\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]E$ and the isomorphism $E\to(M\cap L_\infty)/(M\cap q^{-1}L_\infty)$. Applying step 5.2 with the roles of the charts exchanged gives $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_\infty$.

**Conclusion of (1).** Steps 1.1–6.1 prove all the assertions of (1), including the infinity residue isomorphism and the rational chart extensions $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_0$, $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_\infty$. If $E$ is free with a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis, the tensor identifications exhibit bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$, since $A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z^n\cong A^n$ and similarly for the two chart rings.

**The generation criterion (2).** Let $F$ map into $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, generate $M$ over $A$, and inject into both rational residues. Then $F\cap qL_0=0$ and $F\cap q^{-1}L_\infty=0$, so $F$ is $\mathbb Z$-torsion-free; moreover $M\cap L_0\subseteq F+q(M\cap L_0)$: for $x\in M\cap L_0$ written as a finite $A$-combination of images of $F$, reducing modulo $q(M\cap L_0)$ leaves only the terms of exponent $\le0$, and each such term lies in $F+q(M\cap L_0)$ because the negative-exponent terms are themselves in $L_0$ only through vanishing of their images modulo $q$, which the injection $F\to L_0/qL_0$ forces into $F$. Hence the peeling and termination arguments of steps 2.1, 3.1 and 4.1 apply with $E$ replaced by $F$: $M\cap L_0=\mathbb Z[q]F$, $M=AF=A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}F$ and, by the mirror argument of step 6.1, $M\cap L_\infty=\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]F$ and the maps $F\to L_0/qL_0$, $F\to L_\infty/q^{-1}L_\infty$ are isomorphisms. Then $F\subseteq M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ and $F$ contains, by the peeling, one lift per residue class, so $F=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty=E$ and $E\cong(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$.

**The relative criterion (3): reduction to simultaneous lifts.** Let $N\subseteq M$ with $N\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_N$, $E_N=N\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, and let $F$ be as in (3). Replacing $F$ by a finitely generated submodule and $M$ by $AF+N$ does not change the hypotheses in the required form, so $F$ is a finitely generated torsion-free, hence free, $\mathbb Z$-module. Since $N$ is balanced, $N=(N\cap L_0)+(N\cap L_\infty)$, and one computes $M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)=N+M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$: an element in the left side differs from an element of $M\cap L_0$ by some $n\in N$, whose failure to lie in $L_\infty$ can be split into its $L_0$- and $L_\infty$-chart parts and subtracted.

**Changing the lifts by $N$.** Using step 8.1, each basis element $f\in F$ can be modified by an element of $N$ so that its image lies in $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$; the induced maps $F\to(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$ and to the infinity quotient, together with the injection $E_N\to(N\cap L_0)/(N\cap qL_0)$, show that the direct sum $F\oplus E_N$ injects into both rational residues and generates $M$ over $A$. Applying (2) with this $F\oplus E_N$ gives $M$ balanced, the stated exact sequence and image, and $E_M\cong F\oplus E_N$ when the reduction was finite generated.

**Conclusion.** Step 7.1 gives (1), step 7.2 gives (2), and steps 8.1–9.1 give (3); in every part no containment of charts and no freeness of $M$ was assumed, and freeness of $M$ over $A$ is concluded only from a finite free simultaneous integral basis.

Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, with rational discrete valuation rings $A_0$ at $q=0$ and $A_\infty$ at $q=\infty$. Put $M_A=U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, $L=\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$, and $L^-=\psi(L)$, the bar lattice, as in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]].

The **integral residue lattice** is $L_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L$, a $\mathbb Z[q]$-module, and its **bar lattice** is $L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M_A\cap L^-$, a $\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$-module. The **balanced intersection** is $E_{\mathbb Z}:=M_A\cap L\cap L^-$, a $\mathbb Z$-module. Since $q^{-1}M_A=M_A$, one has $M_A\cap qL=qL_{\mathbb Z}$; consequently the residue map $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to L/qL$ is injective and is $\mathbb Z$-linear. Its image is an integral subgroup of the rational crystal space, not the entire $\mathbb Q$-space. No Laurent-$A$-linearity is asserted on the residue lattice or on the residue map.

The field projection $\pi_\lambda:U_q^-\to V(\lambda)$, $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$, restricts to an $A$-linear surjection $U_A^-\to V_A(\lambda)$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), and it sends $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)$ into $L_{\mathbb Z}(\lambda)$ by the already-proved grand-loop lattice projection ([[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]]). The module $V_A(\lambda)$ is $U_A$-stable: the divided-power and toral reordering identities of [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] reduce the action on $v_\lambda$ to negative divided powers and Gaussian scalars in $A$, with all positive generators killing the highest vector except through the unit, and the residue compatibility of the projection is [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]]. No global freeness, residue spanning or balancedness is assumed here. The integral residue subgroup for the negative half is proved below to be $\mathbb Z B(\infty)$; the module subgroup $\mathbb Z B(\lambda)$ is a consequence of globalization.

Let $U_q^-$ be the negative half of the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its
Kashiwara skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]), let
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A^-$ be the divided-power half generated by
the $F_i^{(r)}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]). Then:

(i) $e_i'$ preserves $U_A^-$: $e_i'(U_A^-)\subseteq U_A^-$.

(ii) Define, for $x\in U_q^-$,
$$P_ix:=\sum_{n\ge0}(-1)^nq_i^{-n(n-1)/2}\,F_i^{(n)}(e_i')^n x,$$
the sum being finite on each $x$ because $e_i'$ is locally nilpotent, and the
powers $(e_i')^n$ being ordinary, not divided, powers of the derivation. Then
$P_i$ is a well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear map with $e_i'P_i=0$ that fixes
$\ker e_i'$ pointwise and annihilates $F_iU_q^-$; hence
$U_q^-=\ker e_i'\oplus F_iU_q^-$ and $P_i$ is the projection onto $\ker e_i'$
along $F_iU_q^-$.

(iii) Every $x\in U_A^-$ has a unique finite expansion
$$x=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n)}x_n,\qquad e_i'x_n=0,$$
with $x_n=q_i^{n(n-1)/2}P_i(e_i')^nx\in U_A^-$ for every $n$; the sum is finite
because $(e_i')^nx=0$ for large $n$. Consequently the string operators
$\tilde e_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge1}F_i^{(n-1)}x_n$ and
$\tilde f_i\bigl(\sum_nF_i^{(n)}x_n\bigr):=\sum_{n\ge0}F_i^{(n+1)}x_n$
preserve $U_A^-$.

No global $A$-basis and no freeness of $U_A^-$ over $A$ is assumed or asserted.

Let $\mathcal L(\infty)\subseteq U_q^-$ and $\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the Kashiwara lattice and generating set of [[def-kashiwara-lattices-lambda-and-infinity]], with the Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-i-string-decomposition-of-the-negative-half]](iii).

(i) $(\mathcal L(\infty),\mathcal B(\infty))$ is a crystal basis of $U_q^-$ in the sense of [[def-crystal-lattice-and-crystal-basis]]: $\mathcal L(\infty)$ is a free $A_0$-submodule with $U_q^-\cong\mathbb Q(q)\otimes_{A_0}\mathcal L(\infty)$, stable under $\tilde e_i$ and $\tilde f_i$; and $\mathcal B(\infty)$ is a $\mathbb Q$-basis of $\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ satisfying $\tilde e_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)\cup\{0\}$, $\tilde f_i\mathcal B(\infty)\subseteq\mathcal B(\infty)$, and $\tilde f_ib=b'$ if and only if $b=\tilde e_ib'$ for all $b,b'\in\mathcal B(\infty)$.

(ii) The root-graded components are free: $\mathcal L(\infty)=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ and each $\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\nu}$ is a free $A_0$-module of rank $\#\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\nu}=\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^-[-\nu]$.

(iii) For every $\lambda\in P^+$ the projection $\pi_\lambda(P)=Pv_\lambda$ maps $\mathcal B(\infty)$ onto $\mathcal B(\lambda)\cup\{0\}$, and the compatibility statements of [[lem-crystal-operators-commute-with-highest-weight-projection-modulo-q]] hold: $\pi_\lambda(\mathcal L(\infty)_{-\alpha})=\mathcal L(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)_{-\alpha}:\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0\}\cong\mathcal B(\lambda)_{\lambda-\alpha}$, $\tilde f_i\pi_\lambda=\pi_\lambda\tilde f_i$ and $\tilde e_i\pi_\lambda(b)=\pi_\lambda(\tilde e_ib)$ whenever $\pi_\lambda(b)\neq0$.

(iv) The root-graded crystal has finite $\varepsilon_i$ on each element, formal $\varphi_i=\varepsilon_i+\langle h_i,\mathrm{wt}\rangle$, and actual lowering length $\ell_i^-=\infty$. Every $\tilde f_i$-iterate is nonzero because $\tilde e_i\tilde f_i=\mathrm{id}$ holds on its lattice and residue. Thus it is the infinite lowering crystal of the unit, with the negative-half convention of the crystal-graph definition.

**Choice.** The axiom of choice is declared via [[def-axiom-of-choice]] and enters only through the grand loop: the partial-inverse axiom in (i) uses clause J(r) of [[thm-grand-loop-existence-of-highest-weight-crystal-bases]], whose proof consumes the AC-dependent form comparison of the negative-half form. The freeness and rank statements are choice-free.

For the highest-module and negative-half Kashiwara lattices, their respective normalized polarizations take values in $A_0$ and their crystal residue bases are orthonormal. On every finite label or root component the Gram determinant is a unit of $A_0$, the $A_0$-pairing is perfect and $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. Moreover $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension of the lattice. These are consequences after the grand loop, not prerequisites for it. Only the field-half supplier's inherited AC hypothesis is retained.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S=\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i'$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$\varepsilon\colon U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the **augmentation**, the projection
onto the degree-zero component $U_q^-[0]=\mathbb Q(q)\cdot1$ (so
$\varepsilon(Q)=0$ on all positive-height components and $\varepsilon(1)=1$).

The **normalized Lusztig–Kashiwara form** on $U_q^-$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon U_q^-\times U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(H) $B$ is **homogeneous**: $B\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu]\bigr)=0$ whenever
$\nu\ne\mu$;

(N) $B(1,1)=1$;

(R) $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ for all $i\in I$ and all $P,Q\in U_q^-$.

Equivalently, axioms (H) and (N) may be replaced by the single **counit
normalization**

(C) $B(1,Q)=\varepsilon(Q)$ for all $Q\in U_q^-$,

in the presence of (R) (Verification, step 1.1).

Axioms (H) and (N) (equivalently (C)) are essential and not redundant: the
recursion (R) together with $B(1,1)=1$ alone neither forces symmetry nor
uniqueness, as the rank-one witness of step 3.1 shows.

The axioms determine $B$ uniquely: peeling first letters in the first argument
writes every positive-height $P$ as a finite sum $P=\sum_iF_iP_i$ and evaluates
$B(P,Q)=\sum_iB(P_i,e_i'Q)$, reducing the height; the base of the induction is
(C) (Verification, step 2.1). The **existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy** of
$B$ on $U_q^-$ for the actual quotient by the Serre ideal are not proved here:
they are the content of the negative-half form theorem
`thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral`,
the declared justification of this definition, which also settles the exact
integrality normalization ($A$-valuedness on the word lattice and the
Gaussian-factorial denominators on the divided-power lattice). That theorem
is proved on this page, and its statement is the declared supplier of
existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy; this definition itself claims only that
(H), (N) and (R) determine $B$ and that the normalization cannot be relaxed.

derivations.claim: **Integral representatives of the crystal basis.** By [F2] every divided-power lowering word $\tilde f_{i_1}\cdots\tilde f_{i_r}\mathbf 1$ lies in $U_A^-$, and by [F3] it lies in $\mathcal L(\infty)$; hence its class lies in $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ and is a nonzero element of $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and every $b\in\mathcal B(\infty)$ is represented by such a word.

**The value rings.** The explicit rank-one divided-word norms $B(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(a)})=1/[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})^{-1}$ and the word Gram expansion of [F5] show that every value on $U_A^-$ is a $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-combination of reciprocal products $\prod(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$ with bounded $r$, i.e. lies in $K_{\mathbb Z}$; and every value on $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ lies in $A_0\cap K_{\mathbb Z}$ by [F4]. The intersection is $A_{\mathbb Z}$: clearing denominators in $A_0\cap K_{\mathbb Z}$ writes the value as a Laurent polynomial with denominator $\prod(1-q^{2n})^{e}$ of constant term $1$, regularity at $q=0$ forces the Laurent polynomial to have no negative powers, and evaluation at $0$ gives an integer. Hence the residue pairing of $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued.

**Integrality of coefficients against representatives.** For $x\in L_{\mathbb Z}$ with rational residue $\sum_ba_bb\in\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$, choose for each $b$ an integral representative $w_b$ of $b$ from step 1.1 and pair modulo $q$: by [F4] the residue form is the positive definite form with orthonormal basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, so $a_b=(x,w_b)$ modulo $q$, and by [F5] this value lies in $A_{\mathbb Z}$; evaluating the resulting $\mathbb Z[q]$-element at $q=0$ gives an integer because $A_{\mathbb Z}$ consists of quotients with denominator $\equiv1\pmod q$. Hence every coefficient $a_b$ is an integer and the image of the injection of [F1] is contained in $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$; conversely finite integer combinations of the classes of the $w_b$ lie in the image, so the image is exactly $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$.

**Norm-one elements.** If $x\in L_{\mathbb Z}$ has residue $\sum_ba_bb$ with $a_b\in\mathbb Z$ by step 2.1 and $B(x,x)=1$, then reducing the positive definite form of [F4] modulo $q$ gives $\sum_ba_b^2=1$; since the $a_b$ are integers, exactly one coefficient is $\pm1$ and all others vanish. Thus $x$ lies in the $\mathbb Z$-span of a single $B$-representative plus $qL_{\mathbb Z}$, and the norm-$1$ elements of $L_{\mathbb Z}$ are exactly the classes of $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$ together with their integral representatives modulo $qL_{\mathbb Z}$; no unsigned statement is made.

**Operator stability and conclusion.** By [F2] and [F3] the operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve both $U_A^-$ and $\mathcal L(\infty)$, hence preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ and descend to the integral residue subgroup, which by steps 1.1–1.2 is the free $\mathbb Z$-module $\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb$; tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ gives the full rational crystal space by [F3]. Together with steps 2.1 and 3.1 this proves all the assertions, with the stated $\mathbb Z$-valued pairing and signed norm-$1$ characterization.

citations.quote: For the highest-module and negative-half Kashiwara lattices, their respective normalized polarizations take values in $A_0$ and their crystal residue bases are orthonormal. On every finite label or root component the Gram determinant is a unit of $A_0$, the $A_0$-pairing is perfect and $\mathcal L^\vee=\mathcal L$. Moreover $\mathcal L=\{x:\langle x,x\rangle\in A_0\}$ inside the field scalar extension of the lattice. These are consequences after the grand loop, not prerequisites for it. Only the field-half supplier's inherited AC hypothesis is retained.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S=\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $L_{\mathbb Z}(\infty)=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$ be the integral residue lattice of [[def-integral-residue-lattices-of-the-negative-half-and-highest-weight-modules]], with $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}\to\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$ the canonical injection. Then the image of this injection is exactly $\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B(\infty)}\mathbb Z b$; in particular $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is a free $\mathbb Z$-module with basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$, and after tensoring with $\mathbb Q$ it is the full rational crystal space $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\bigoplus_b\mathbb Zb=\mathcal L(\infty)/q\mathcal L(\infty)$.

The normalized Kashiwara half form of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] takes values on $U_A^-$ in $K_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1},(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$ and on $L_{\mathbb Z}$ in $A_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Z[q,(1-q^{2n})^{-1}:n\ge1]$; consequently its residue pairing on $L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}$ is $\mathbb Z$-valued. In the residue basis $\mathcal B(\infty)$ the coefficients of an integral element are its integer pairings with the basis vectors, and the elements of $L_{\mathbb Z}$ of norm $1$ are exactly $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$. The Kashiwara operators $\tilde e_i,\tilde f_i$ preserve $L_{\mathbb Z}$, hence induce endomorphisms of the integral residue subgroup. No $A$-module structure on $L_{\mathbb Z}$, no identification of the integral residue with the rational residue as a $\mathbb Z$-module, and no unsigned norm-$1$ characterization is asserted; the module integral residue basis is established only in the globalization theorem of this page.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

derivations.claim: **$\star$ is a well-defined anti-involution.** The assignment $F_i\mapsto F_i$ extended antimultiplicatively is defined on the free algebra, and applying it to a negative Serre relation $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r=0$ and reversing the order of each monomial gives $\sum_r(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{r}F_jF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}$, which is the same sum after the substitution $r\mapsto1-a_{ij}-r$ and the exact symmetry $\binom{m}{r}_i=\binom{m}{m-r}_i$ of the Gaussian binomials. Hence $\star$ descends to $U_q^-$, fixes $F_i$, and is an anti-involution: it reverses words and its square is the identity.

**Integral and bar compatibility.** Since $\star$ fixes each divided power $F_i^{(r)}$ (it fixes $F_i$ and the scalar $[r]_i!$), it maps each generator of $U_A^-$ to a generator, so $\star(U_A^-)=U_A^-$. It commutes with $\psi$ because both are $\mathbb Q(q)$-semilinear, $\star$ fixes $q$ while $\psi$ sends $q\mapsto q^{-1}$, and on generators $\psi\star(F_i)=\psi(F_i)=F_i=\star\psi(F_i)$.

**Isometry for the half form.** Write $P=F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_r}$, $Q=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_s}$ as words. Reversing both words, $P^\star=F_{i_r}\cdots F_{i_1}$, $Q^\star=F_{j_s}\cdots F_{j_1}$, and the word Gram formula of [F1] expands both $B(P,Q)$ and $B(P^\star,Q^\star)$ as sums over bijections between matched colors with the same crossing exponents read backwards; reversing a permutation preserves the weight and the crossing number, so the two sums are termwise equal. Hence $B(P^\star,Q^\star)=B(P,Q)$ on words and, by bilinearity and descent through the Serre ideal, on all of $U_q^-$.

**Lattice stability.** For $P\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ one has $B(P^\star,P^\star)=B(P,P)\in A_0$ by step 2.1 and the norm characterization of [F1]; hence $P^\star\in\mathcal L(\infty)$ and $\star$ preserves $\mathcal L(\infty)$. It preserves $U_A^-$ by step 1.2, so it preserves $L_{\mathbb Z}=U_A^-\cap\mathcal L(\infty)$; since it commutes with $\psi$ and $\psi(L_{\mathbb Z})=L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, it also preserves the bar lattice $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$.

**The signed residue permutation.** For $x\in L_{\mathbb Z}$ with residue $\sum_ba_bb$, the residue of $x^\star$ is $\sum_ba_b'b$ where the coefficients are determined by the orthonormal residue pairing; because the residue pairing is invariant under $\star$ by step 2.1, $a_b'=a_b$ up to the index permutation induced by a signed bijection of the basis: by the signed norm characterization of [F2], if $x$ has norm $1$ then $x^\star$ has norm $1$, so $\star$ maps the set of signed basis classes $\mathcal B(\infty)\cup(-\mathcal B(\infty))$ to itself, permuting it.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 prove that $\star$ is an anti-involution preserving $U_A^-$ and commuting with bar, step 2.1 proves that it is an isometry of the normalized half form, step 3.1 proves preservation of $\mathcal L(\infty)$, $L_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-$, and step 4.1 gives the signed permutation of the integral crystal residue. No unsigned star-crystal theorem is asserted.
