Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

The two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $q$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$$A_0:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}=\Big\{\frac fg\ :\ f,g\in\mathbb Q[q],\ g(0)\neq0\Big\}\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$$
be the localisation of the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q[q]$ at the prime ideal $(q)$ ([[def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal]]). By [[ex-the-local-ring-of-polynomials-at-x]] with $F=\mathbb Q$, the ring $A_0$ is exactly the ring of rational functions regular at $q=0$, it is a local ring ([[def-local-ring]]) with unique maximal ideal $qA_0$, and evaluation at $0$ induces an isomorphism $A_0/qA_0\cong\mathbb Q$. Since $\mathbb Q[q]$ is a principal ideal domain ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-pid]]) with nonzero prime ideal $(q)$, the ring $A_0$ is a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal; by the discrete valuation ring characterisations it is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser $q/1$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]], [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), and in particular a principal ideal domain ([[cor-dvr-is-a-pid]], [[def-principal-ideal-domain]]), with field of fractions $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[cor-rational-function-field-as-a-fraction-field]]).

By [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]] a discrete valuation ring is the valuation ring $V_v=\{x:v(x)\ge0\}$ of a discrete valuation $v$ on its fraction field. The discrete valuation of $\mathbb Q(q)$ with $V_v=A_0$ and $v(q)=1$ is the **$q$-adic valuation**; write it $\operatorname{ord}_q$, so that
$$\operatorname{ord}_q:\mathbb Q(q)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z\cup\{\infty\},\qquad A_0=\{h\in\mathbb Q(q):\operatorname{ord}_q(h)\ge0\},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_q(q)=1 .$$
Equivalently, $\operatorname{ord}_q$ is the vanishing order at $q=0$. The units of $A_0$ are exactly the fractions $f/g$ with $f(0)\neq0$ and $g(0)\neq0$, and $qA_0$ is the maximal ideal, so $q$ is a uniformiser of $A_0$ ([[thm-localisation-at-a-prime-is-local]]).

This ring $A_0$ is the **crystal limiting ring** of the crystal development below, and it is different from the Laurent ring $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ of [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]: $q^{-1}\in A\setminus A_0$, while $(1+q)^{-1}\in A_0\setminus A$; neither ring contains the other, and both are subrings of $\mathbb Q(q)$. For every free $A_0$-module $L$ the canonical map
$$\mathbb Q\otimes_{A_0}L\longrightarrow L/qL,\qquad c\otimes\ell\mapsto c\,\ell+qL,$$
is an isomorphism, and for every $\lambda\in\mathbb Q(q)^\times$ one has $\lambda L/q\lambda L\cong L/qL$; passing from $L$ to $L/qL$ is the **crystal limit**. No freeness of any further module, no lattice and no choice principle is asserted here.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

derivations.claim: **Witness (1): the balanced intersection and the missing residue class.** Write $a:=v+w$ and $t:=v$, so $L'=A_0a\oplus qA_0t$ and $V_A=Av\oplus Aw=\mathbb Q(q)$-span; since $w=a-t$ and $v=t$. An element $\alpha a+\beta t$ with $\alpha\in A_0$, $\beta\in qA_0$ lies in $V_A=Av\oplus Aw$ exactly when $\alpha\in A_0\cap A=\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\beta\in qA_0\cap A=qZ[q]$, so $V_A\cap L'=\mathbb Z[q]a\oplus q\mathbb Z[q]t$. Similarly $\psi(L')=A_\infty a\oplus q^{-1}A_\infty t$, and the triple intersection is $$E_{\mathbb Z}=V_A\cap L'\cap\psi(L')=\bigl(\mathbb Z[q]\cap\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\bigr)a\oplus\bigl(q\mathbb Z[q]\cap q^{-1}\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\bigr)t=\mathbb Z a,$$ by [L4]. The integral residue of the zero chart is $(V_A\cap L')/(V_A\cap qL')=\mathbb Z[q]a/q\mathbb Z[q]a\oplus q\mathbb Z[q]t/q^2\mathbb Z[q]t$, which contains the nonzero class $qt+qL'=qv+qL'$. The balanced map sends $\mathbb Za$ onto the classes of integer multiples of $a$ and therefore misses that class, so the triple is not balanced by [L1].

**Witness (2): the rank-three balanced intersection.** For the trivial module $L''=q^{-1}A_0v$, so $V_A\cap L''=q^{-1}Z[q]v$ by [L4], and $\psi(L'')=qA_\infty v$, so $V_A\cap\psi(L'')=qA_\infty v\cap Av$. An element of $V_A\cap L''$ is $q^{-1}fv$ with $f\in\mathbb Z[q]$, and it lies in $qA_\infty v$ exactly when $q^{-1}f\in A_\infty$, i.e. when $f\in q\mathbb Z[q]$; hence $$E_{\mathbb Z}=V_A\cap L''\cap\psi(L'')=\mathbb Zq^{-1}v\oplus\mathbb Zv\oplus\mathbb Zqv,$$ the three Laurent monomials being exactly the integer-coefficient combinations with exponents between $-1$ and $1$.

**Witness (1): the lattice defects.** The vector $a=v+w$ is fixed by $\psi$, since $\psi(v)=v$, $\psi(w)=w$ and $\psi(q)=q^{-1}$ only acts on coefficients, and it lies in $L'$ with residue class $a+qL'$. But $a$ is a sum of two weight vectors of different weights, so $L'$ is not weight decomposed, and $\tilde e a=v\notin L'$ because $v=\beta t$ would require $\beta=1\notin qA_0$; thus $L'$ fails the crystal-lattice axioms of [L2] and the bar-fixed vector alone provides no parametrization or uniqueness.

**Witness (2): the kernel and the two lifts.** Since $V_A\cap qL''=q(q^{-1}Z[q])v=\mathbb Z[q]v$, the integral globalization map $E_{\mathbb Z}\to(V_A\cap L'')/(V_A\cap qL'')=\mathbb Z[q]v/q\mathbb Z[q]v$ is $(a_{-1}q^{-1}+a_0+a_1q)v\mapsto a_{-1}[v]$, which is onto with kernel $\mathbb Zv\oplus\mathbb Zqv\ne0$. The elements $g_1=(q+q^{-1})v$ and $g_2=(q+q^{-1})v+v=(q+q^{-1}+1)v$ both lie in $E_{\mathbb Z}$, both are fixed by $\psi$ because $\psi(q+q^{-1})=q+q^{-1}$ and $\psi(v)=v$, and both have residue class $q^{-1}v+qL''$; they are distinct since $g_2-g_1=v\ne0$. Hence the same nonzero crystal residue has two distinct bar-fixed integral lifts, and bar invariance plus congruence does not give uniqueness without the balanced isomorphism.

**Witness (2) is a genuine crystal lattice.** In the trivial module all Kashiwara operators vanish and $L''=q^{-1}A_0v$ is a full free $A_0$-lattice with residue generator $q^{-1}v+qL''$; by [L2] it is a crystal lattice, so the failure of uniqueness in step 2.2 is not attributable to an invalid lattice. The genuine Kashiwara triples of [L5] require and possess the actual integral balanced map, which the present lattices do not have; accordingly no claim of the globalization theorem is contradicted.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 exhibit the nonbalanced lattice $L'$ whose bar-fixed vector $v+w$ cannot be globalized onto the residue class $qv+qL'$; steps 2.1–3.1 exhibit a valid crystal lattice with two distinct bar-fixed integral lifts of one nonzero crystal residue. Both conclusions are established by explicit coefficient computations in the displayed modules.

boundaries.evidence: Step 1.1 computes the balanced intersection of the mixed lattice directly; no empty coefficient range occurs because all coefficients are Laurent polynomials.
Step 1.2 computes the rank-three intersection with the inverse-power coefficient normalized, and no division by a vanishing scalar occurs since $q$ is a unit.

boundaries.reason: The argument contains no instance of this boundary case: it is a direct structural or coefficientwise computation over finite root or label components, with no empty, degenerate, endpoint or biconditional hypothesis.

boundaries.evidence: Step 3.1 treats the two distinct lifts differing by a nonzero vector, the degenerate coincidence case of the balanced map.
The coefficient bounds of the counterexample are finite Laurent-degree bounds, computed in steps 1.1 and 1.2.
The counterexample displays all lattices and lifts explicitly; no element is selected from a family, and the cited suppliers are used only for notation.
Step 1.1 proves that the residue class of $qv$ lies outside the image of the balanced map, the failure of the forward implication.
Step 3.1 produces two distinct bar-fixed lifts of one residue class, the failure of the reverse uniqueness direction.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum and let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with $q_i=q^{d_i}$, $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, coproduct $\Delta$, counit $\varepsilon$ and antipode $S$ as in [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]]. Write $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and let $U_A$, with generators $E_i^{(r)},F_i^{(r)},K_h^{\pm1},T_{i,c,t}$, be the Lusztig divided-power form of the receiving page. On the source side take Lusztig's presentation in the parameter $v$ with $v_i=q_i^{-1}$: generators $E_i^{L},F_i^{L},K_h^{L}$, the toral relations $K_h^{L}K_{h'}^{L}=K_{h+h'}^{L}$, $K_0^{L}=1$, the toral-action relations
$$K_h^{L}E_i^{L}=v^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_i^{L}K_h^{L},\qquad K_h^{L}F_i^{L}=v^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_i^{L}K_h^{L},$$
the mixed relations $E_i^{L}F_j^{L}-F_j^{L}E_i^{L}=\delta_{ij}(K_i^{L}-(K_i^{L})^{-1})/(v_i-v_i^{-1})$, and the Serre relations with $v_i$-Gaussian binomial coefficients; let $\Delta_L$ be the source coproduct on generators
$$\Delta_L E_i^{L}=E_i^{L}\otimes1+K_i^{L}\otimes E_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L F_i^{L}=F_i^{L}\otimes(K_i^{L})^{-1}+1\otimes F_i^{L},\qquad \Delta_L K_h^{L}=K_h^{L}\otimes K_h^{L}.$$
Let $B_K$ be the normalized Kashiwara half form on $U_q^-$ of [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]], with skew derivations $e_i',e_i''$ of [[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], and let $\psi$ be the bar involution of [[lem-the-lusztig-integral-form-is-stable-under-bar-and-contravariant-duality]]. Then:

(i) **Parameter transport.** The assignment $\varphi(q)=q^{-1}$, $\varphi(E_i)=E_i$, $\varphi(F_i)=F_i$, $\varphi(K_h)=K_h^{-1}=K_{-h}$, extended semilinearly ( $\varphi(\lambda x)=\lambda|_{q\mapsto q^{-1}}\varphi(x)$ ) and multiplicatively, is a semilinear algebra involution of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$: it carries every source relation above to a relation of the library presentation and conversely, so it identifies the two presentations and is the bar involution $\psi$; and $\varphi(U_A)=U_A$ with $\varphi(E_i^{(r)})=E_i^{(r)}$, $\varphi(F_i^{(r)})=F_i^{(r)}$, $\varphi(K_h^{\pm1})=K_h^{\mp1}$, $\varphi(T_{i,c,t})=T_{i,c,t}$.

(ii) **Coproduct transport.** On all of the source algebra, $(\varphi\otimes\varphi)\circ\Delta_L=\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\circ\varphi$, where $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}=\mathrm{flip}\circ\Delta$. Equivalently the source coproduct is the opposite of the fixed library coproduct after parameter transport: the flip of the transported source coproduct is $\Delta$. In particular, with the barred coproduct $\bar\Delta(u):=(\psi\otimes\psi)\Delta(\psi(u))$, an element of the completed tensor square satisfying the source intertwining convention for $\Delta_L$ has a transport-flip that satisfies the library convention $\Delta(u)\Theta=\Theta\bar\Delta(u)$; this is the convention under which the normalized family of (vi) is read.

(iii) **The abstract half and its twisted product.** Transporting $\theta_i\mapsto F_i$ sends the source half $\mathbf f$ to $U_q^-$, the divided powers $\theta_i^{(n)}$ to $F_i^{(n)}$, and the source twisted coproduct multiplication $(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=v^{\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$ to
$$(x_1\otimes x_2)(y_1\otimes y_2)=q^{-\langle\deg x_2,\deg y_1\rangle}x_1y_1\otimes x_2y_2$$
on $U_q^-\otimes U_q^-$; the coefficient extraction $e_i'(F_jQ)=\delta_{ij}Q+q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(Q)$ of the transported twisted coproduct agrees with the library skew derivation $e_i'$.

(iv) **The half form up to the root-color factor.** On the homogeneous degree $\nu=\sum_i\nu_i\alpha_i$ the source form and the normalized Kashiwara form are related by
$$B_L=C_\nu\,B_K,\qquad C_\nu=\prod_i(1-q_i^2)^{-\nu_i},$$
a color-degree scaling which is a unit congruent to $1$ modulo $q$ and is not a single scalar on the whole half; for $P,Q$ of different degrees both sides vanish. In the rank-one subalgebra $B_L(F_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q_i^{2r})^{-1}$.

(v) **The normalized Drinfeld pairing.** Let $\iota:U_q^+\to U_q^-$ be the algebra isomorphism $E_i\mapsto F_i$. On homogeneous elements of opposite degrees set
$$D(x,y)=d_\nu^{-1}B_K(\iota x,y),\qquad d_\nu=\prod_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})^{\nu_i}\ \ (\deg x=\nu,\ \deg y=-\nu),$$
and set $D(x,y)=0$ for degrees not opposite. Then $D$ is a well-defined homogeneous pairing, perfect on every finite graded piece, and $D(E_i,F_j)=\delta_{ij}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$; the pairing with generator value $1$ is the $B_K$-transport $B_K(\iota x,y)$. Its divided-power values are
$$D(E_i^{(n)},F_i^{(n)})=\frac{q_i^{-n(n-1)/2}}{[n]_i!\,(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n}.$$

(vi) **Quasi-R normalization.** In each degree $\nu$ let $(x_a),(y_b)$ be bases of $U_q^+[\nu]$ and $U_q^-[-\nu]$ and let $\Theta_\nu=\sum_a x_a\otimes y^a$ be the $D$-coevaluation, $y^a$ the $D$-dual basis. Then $\Theta_\nu$ is the transported, tensor-flipped source quasi-R component: the source coefficient of Lusztig's printed $\Theta$ is $(-1)^{\mathrm{ht}\,\nu}\prod_iv_i^{\nu_i}$ times the $B_L$-coevaluation, and after parameter transport and flip this scalar equals $d_\nu$, the scalar by which the $D$-coevaluation differs from the $B_K$-coevaluation. In particular, writing $[n]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{r=1}^n(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(r-1)})$ (the geometric-sum factorial of the receiving page),
$$\Theta_{n\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})^n[n]_{q_i^2}!\,E_i^{(n)}\otimes F_i^{(n)},\qquad\text{so}\qquad \Theta_{\alpha_i}=(q_i-q_i^{-1})\,E_i\otimes F_i.$$

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld-Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), with skew derivations
$e_i',e_i''$ ([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]),
and let $(\ ,\ )$ be a bilinear form on $U_q^-$.

(i) **Existence and symmetry.** A bilinear form with $(1,1)=1$ and
$(F_iP,Q)=(P,e_i'(Q))$ for all $i,P,Q$ exists on $U_q^-$; every normalized
homogeneous form satisfying these conditions is symmetric; and by the
uniqueness of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]]
there is exactly one such form. No separate right-adjunction formula for
$(P,QF_i)$ is asserted: in the rank-one subalgebra a formula
$(P,QF_i)=c\,(e_i''P,Q)$ with constant $c$ is false, as the explicit values in
(iv) show.

(ii) **Orthogonality.** $(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu])=0$ whenever $\nu\ne\mu$.

(iii) **Nondegeneracy.** For every $0\ne x\in U_q^-$ there is $y\in U_q^-$ with
$(x,y)\ne0$; equivalently, the restriction of the form to each
finite-dimensional graded piece $U_q^-[-\nu]$ is nondegenerate.

(iv) **Integrality on the word lattice.** Let $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]) and let $W\subseteq U_A^-$ be the
$A$-span of the monomials $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$ ($k\ge0$). Then
$W\subseteq U_A^-$ (because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ and $[k]_i!\in A$), and
$(W,W)\subseteq A$. On the larger divided-power lattice $U_A^-$ the form is
*not* $A$-valued: in the rank-one subalgebra generated by a single $F_i$ one
has, for all $a,b\ge0$,
$$(F_i^{(a)},F_i^{(b)})=\delta_{ab}\frac{q_i^{-a(a-1)/2}}{[a]_i!}=\delta_{ab}\frac{1}{[a]_{q_i^2}!},$$
in particular $(F_i^{(2)},F_i^{(2)})=1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$; here
$[a]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{m=1}^a(1+q_i^2+\cdots+q_i^{2(m-1)})$. Globally, with
$A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$, the localization of $A$ inverting the
multiplicative set $S=\{[r]_i!:i\in I,r\ge1\}$ (equivalently inverting the
Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$), one has
$(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}$: divided-power words are word
vectors divided by finite products of these factorials. This is an exact
denominator bound, not an $A$-integrality assertion on $U_A^-$ in this
normalization.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

For the divided-power integral form $U_A^-$ of [[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]] and for every dominant $\lambda$, let $M_A$ be $U_A^-$ or $V_A(\lambda)=U_A^-v_\lambda$, let $L$ be $\mathcal L(\infty)$ or $\mathcal L(\lambda)$ with bar lattice $L^-=\psi(L)$, and let $\mathcal B$ be $\mathcal B(\infty)$ or $\mathcal B(\lambda)$. Then there is a unique lower global family $G(\mathcal B)\subseteq M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ with the property that the residue class of $G(b)$ in $(M_A\cap L)/(M_A\cap qL)$ is $b$ for every $b\in\mathcal B$, namely the family of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]]. It is bar invariant, a genuine $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ basis of $M_A$, and a basis of both rational chart lattices $L$ and $L^-$ over $A_0$ and $A_\infty$; its $\mathbb Z$-span is the simultaneous balanced intersection $M_A\cap L\cap L^-$ and its field span is the whole module. It is adapted to every divided string-image ideal in the exact sense of the integral balanced theorem, and the same family is obtained with residue $b$ over either chart. No word family is assumed to be a basis, no unitriangular characterization is used, and no lower lattice self-duality is asserted.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

derivations.claim: **Rank one.** By [L1] the lower global vector of the $n$-th class is $F^{(n)}$, bar fixed and congruent to it; by [L2] its Kashiwara norm is $1/[n]_{q^2}!$ and its Lusztig norm is the color-factor multiple $\prod_{r=1}^n(1-q^{2r})^{-1}=(1-q^2)^{-n}/[n]_{q^2}!$. Since $F^n=[n]_q!F^{(n)}$ and $[n]_q!$ is not a unit of $A$ for $n\ge2$, the ordinary power differs by a nonunit, and the Drinfeld generator pairing value $1/(q-q^{-1})$ records the remaining scalar.

**The two mixed $A_2$ vectors are lifts.** By [L3] the classes $\tilde f_1\tilde f_2\mathbf 1$ and $\tilde f_2\tilde f_1\mathbf 1$ equal $F_1F_2$ and $F_2F_1$; both are integral (products of generators), bar fixed ($\psi$ fixes each $F_i$ and reverses no letters here since $\psi$ is an algebra automorphism fixing $F_i$), and congruent to their distinct crystal residues, so by [L4] they are exactly the lower global lifts with no correction.

**The Gram matrices.** The diagonal pairings are $1$ by the normalization of the half form; the cross pairing $\langle F_1F_2,F_2F_1\rangle$ is computed by the adjunction with $e_1'$, using $e_1'(F_2F_1)=qF_2$ from [L3], giving $q$. Hence the Kashiwara Gram matrix is $\begin{pmatrix}1&q\\q&1\end{pmatrix}$ with determinant $1-q^2$, and the transported Lusztig Gram matrix is its color-factor multiple $(1-q^2)^{-2}$ times it.

**Upper duals and the last degree.** Inverting the field Gram matrix gives the two displayed upper dual vectors, which are not the lower basis vectors; the reciprocal color factor multiplies the Lusztig form-duals by $(1-q^2)^2$. In degree $2\alpha_1$ the only class is that of $F_1^{(2)}$, whose norm is the rank-one value of step 1.1.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–3.1 exhibit the exact normalizations in rank one and in degree $\alpha_1+\alpha_2$ of $A_2$, the absence of triangular corrections in that degree, and the explicitly non-unimodular inverse-Gram duals. All displayed matrices and scalars are finite computations, and no false Gram-unimodularity is asserted.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 4.1), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 5.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $M=\bigoplus_\mu M_\mu$ be $U_q^-$ or an integrable highest weight module $V(\lambda)$, with finite root or label components, lower global $A$-lattice $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A)_\mu=\bigoplus_{b\in\mathcal B}AG(b)$ of [[def-lower-global-basis-of-a-quantum-highest-weight-module]] with rational lower charts $L_0$, $L_\infty=\psi(L_0)$ of the balanced triple [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]], and let $B$ be the normalized homogeneous Kashiwara half form, respectively the contravariant polarization of [[def-the-lusztig-kashiwara-bilinear-form-on-the-negative-quantum-half]], [[thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral]] and [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

The **restricted graded integral form-dual** of $M_A$ is
$$M_A^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(M_A)_\mu)\subseteq A\},$$
the direct sum being taken over weight components so that ordinary (not product) duals of the infinite-dimensional pieces are used; the **dual rational charts** are
$$L_0^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_0)_\mu)\subseteq A_0\},\qquad L_\infty^\vee:=\bigoplus_\mu\{x\in M_\mu:B(x,(L_\infty)_\mu)\subseteq A_\infty\}.$$
The **upper global family** is the unique homogeneous field family $G^{\mathrm{up}}(b)$ ($b\in\mathcal B$) determined by the inverse Gram system
$$B(G(b'),G^{\mathrm{up}}(b))=\delta_{b,b'}\qquad(b,b'\in\mathcal B_\mu);$$
it is defined componentwise by finite-dimensional linear algebra because each component form is nondegenerate. The **upper bar** $\psi^\vee$ is the $B$-adjoint semilinear involution characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$, and the **upper Kashiwara operators** are the adjoints $\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$ and $\tilde f_i^{\mathrm{up}}:=(\tilde e_i^{\mathrm{low}})^{\mathrm{adj}}$, defined componentwise by the same nondegenerate finite-dimensional forms; they are in general distinct from the lower operators.

The upper zero chart is the dual chart $L_0^\vee$, and after the grand loop its perfection identifies it with $L_0$; the upper infinity chart $L_\infty^\vee$ is not automatically the lower bar chart $L_\infty$, and no such identification is asserted. Existence of the upper family in the integral lattices, weightwise perfect $A$-duality, dual globalization in these genuine dual charts and crystal compatibility for the adjoint operators are the exact conclusions of [[thm-upper-and-lower-global-bases-are-dual-and-crystal-compatible]]; adjacent divided-string formulas of the next lemma supply the adjoints of the lower string shifts with their weights, so no unweighted adjunction, no full product identification $M_A^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_A,A)$, no lower $A$-self-duality, no ordinary-bar fixedness and no unqualified upper/lower operator equality is assumed here.

derivations.claim: **The norms.** The recurrence of [L1] with base $d_{m,0}=1$ gives the diagonal values; iterating it produces the closed form $d_{m,n}=q^{n(m-n)}\binom{m}{n}_q$ of [L2], and orthogonality between distinct labels makes the Gram matrix diagonal.

**Common crystal lattice and residues.** Since $1+q^2$ is a unit of $A_0$ congruent to $1$ modulo $q$, both $M_A$ and $M_A^\vee$ extend to the same $A_0$-lattice, and the residues of $w_n$ and $w_n^{\mathrm{up}}$ are the same crystal class $b_n$; the upper operators are the weighted adjoints whose $q=0$ reductions reproduce the same partial-inverse string, while exact adjunction carries the ratios $d_{m,n}/d_{m,n\pm1}$ given by the duality theorem and therefore holds only modulo $q$, not exactly over $\mathbb Q(q)$.

**Bars.** The ordinary bar fixes $w_1$ but sends its upper denominator to $1+q^{-2}$, so it moves $w_1^{\mathrm{up}}$; the adjoint bar $\psi^\vee$ is characterized by $B(\psi u,\psi^\vee v)=\overline{B(u,v)}$ and, on the diagonal form, fixes each $w_n^{\mathrm{up}}$. This is exactly the distinction between lower-bar and adjoint-bar fixedness asserted by the duality theorem, and no lower/upper basis equality is implied.

**The two lattices for $m=2$.** Substituting $m=2$: $d_{2,0}=1$, $d_{2,1}=q\binom{2}{1}_q=q(q+q^{-1})=1+q^2$, $d_{2,2}=1$. Hence $M_A=\bigoplus Aw_n$ and $M_A^\vee=Aw_0\oplus A(1+q^2)^{-1}w_1\oplus Aw_2$, whose middle coefficient module $A/(1+q^2)$ is nonzero; in particular $M_A^\vee$ properly contains $M_A$ and the inclusion is not an isomorphism. For $m=1$, $d_{1,0}=d_{1,1}=1$ and the two lattices coincide.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–2.1 compute the rank-one norms, compare the two genuine $A$-lattices, exhibit the common crystal lattice and residues with only modulo-$q$ adjoint agreement, and identify the correct bar. All calculations are finite and use no determinant-unit assumption.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subseteq V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be free full rational chart lattices over $A_0,A_\infty$ (as for a based module in [[def-the-bar-lattice-and-integral-lattice-of-a-based-module]]). Put
$$L_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0,\qquad L_{\mathbb Z}^-:=M\cap L_\infty,\qquad E_{\mathbb Z}:=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty.$$
The **integral triple** $(M,L_0,L_\infty)$ is **balanced** if the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map
$$E_{\mathbb Z}\longrightarrow L_{\mathbb Z}/qL_{\mathbb Z}=(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$$
is an isomorphism. Its inverse is the **integral globalization map** on the integral residue subgroup. **Rational balancedness** is the corresponding isomorphism $\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}\to L_0/qL_0$, after extending the integral subgroup by $\mathbb Q$. In the applications of this page the integral subgroup is $\mathbb Z B$ for the lower global family $B$, and its globalization gives the lower lifts $G(b)$.

The two-chart lemma of this page proves $M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$, $L_{\mathbb Z}\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$ and $L_{\mathbb Z}^-\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_{\mathbb Z}$. If $E_{\mathbb Z}$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis $B_E$ whose rational residue classes are a basis of $L_0/qL_0$, these lifts give bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$ respectively. Thus $A$-freeness of $M$ is a conclusion from integral balancedness together with a proved free integral residue basis; it is not automatic for an arbitrary not-finitely-generated $\mathbb Z$-submodule. All definitions apply componentwise to the finite root or label spaces.

Let $V$ be finite-dimensional over $\mathbb Q(q)$, let $M\subset V$ be an $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-submodule spanning $V$, and let $L_0,L_\infty$ be full free $A_0$- and $A_\infty$-lattices in $V$. Write $E=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ and use the balanced-triple language of [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]].

(1) If the canonical $\mathbb Z$-linear map $E\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$ is an isomorphism, then
$$M\cap L_0\cong\mathbb Z[q]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cap L_\infty\cong\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,\qquad M\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E,$$
and the infinity residue map $E\to(M\cap L_\infty)/(M\cap q^{-1}L_\infty)$ is also an isomorphism; moreover $A_0\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_0$ and $A_\infty\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E\cong L_\infty$ under the maps induced by inclusions. If $E$ has a finite $\mathbb Z$-basis, these are actual free bases of $M,L_0,L_\infty$ over $A,A_0,A_\infty$. No containment $M\subset L_0\cap L_\infty$ and no freeness of $M/E$ is assumed.

(2) If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps into $M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, generates $M$ over $A$, and maps injectively into both rational residues $L_0/qL_0$ and $L_\infty/q^{-1}L_\infty$, then $F\cong E\cong(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)$.

(3) More generally, let $N\subset M$ be an $A$-submodule whose integral intersection $E_N=N\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$ satisfies $N\cong A\otimes_{\mathbb Z}E_N$. If a $\mathbb Z$-module $F$ maps to $M\cap(L_0+N)\cap(L_\infty+N)$, generates $M$ modulo $N$ over $A$, and maps injectively into $(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$ and $(L_\infty+\mathbb QN)/(q^{-1}L_\infty+\mathbb QN)$, then $M$ is balanced. The sequence
$$0\to(N\cap L_0)/(N\cap qL_0)\to(M\cap L_0)/(M\cap qL_0)\to(L_0+\mathbb QN)/(qL_0+\mathbb QN)$$
is exact, and its last image is the image of $F$. If $F$ and $E_N$ are finite free $\mathbb Z$-modules, then so is $E_M=M\cap L_0\cap L_\infty$, and $M$ is free over $A$.

These are the integral forms of Kashiwara's chart lemmas, in the notation of [[def-balanced-triple-and-globalization-map]]; their rational base extension gives the usual $A_0/A_\infty$ criterion, and no containment of charts or freeness of $M$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $q$ be transcendental over $\mathbb Q$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$$A_0:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q)}=\Big\{\frac fg\ :\ f,g\in\mathbb Q[q],\ g(0)\neq0\Big\}\subseteq\mathbb Q(q)$$
be the localisation of the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q[q]$ at the prime ideal $(q)$ ([[def-localisation-at-a-prime-ideal]]). By [[ex-the-local-ring-of-polynomials-at-x]] with $F=\mathbb Q$, the ring $A_0$ is exactly the ring of rational functions regular at $q=0$, it is a local ring ([[def-local-ring]]) with unique maximal ideal $qA_0$, and evaluation at $0$ induces an isomorphism $A_0/qA_0\cong\mathbb Q$. Since $\mathbb Q[q]$ is a principal ideal domain ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-field-is-a-pid]]) with nonzero prime ideal $(q)$, the ring $A_0$ is a local principal ideal domain with nonzero maximal ideal; by the discrete valuation ring characterisations it is a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser $q/1$ ([[thm-equivalent-characterisations-of-a-dvr]], [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]), and in particular a principal ideal domain ([[cor-dvr-is-a-pid]], [[def-principal-ideal-domain]]), with field of fractions $\mathbb Q(q)$ ([[cor-rational-function-field-as-a-fraction-field]]).

By [[def-discrete-valuation-ring]] a discrete valuation ring is the valuation ring $V_v=\{x:v(x)\ge0\}$ of a discrete valuation $v$ on its fraction field. The discrete valuation of $\mathbb Q(q)$ with $V_v=A_0$ and $v(q)=1$ is the **$q$-adic valuation**; write it $\operatorname{ord}_q$, so that
$$\operatorname{ord}_q:\mathbb Q(q)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z\cup\{\infty\},\qquad A_0=\{h\in\mathbb Q(q):\operatorname{ord}_q(h)\ge0\},\qquad \operatorname{ord}_q(q)=1 .$$
Equivalently, $\operatorname{ord}_q$ is the vanishing order at $q=0$. The units of $A_0$ are exactly the fractions $f/g$ with $f(0)\neq0$ and $g(0)\neq0$, and $qA_0$ is the maximal ideal, so $q$ is a uniformiser of $A_0$ ([[thm-localisation-at-a-prime-is-local]]).

This ring $A_0$ is the **crystal limiting ring** of the crystal development below, and it is different from the Laurent ring $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ of [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]: $q^{-1}\in A\setminus A_0$, while $(1+q)^{-1}\in A_0\setminus A$; neither ring contains the other, and both are subrings of $\mathbb Q(q)$. For every free $A_0$-module $L$ the canonical map
$$\mathbb Q\otimes_{A_0}L\longrightarrow L/qL,\qquad c\otimes\ell\mapsto c\,\ell+qL,$$
is an isomorphism, and for every $\lambda\in\mathbb Q(q)^\times$ one has $\lambda L/q\lambda L\cong L/qL$; passing from $L$ to $L/qL$ is the **crystal limit**. No freeness of any further module, no lattice and no choice principle is asserted here.

For any finite sequence of based integrable modules in the finite-weight-space category $O_{\mathrm{int}}$, the field tensor bar $\Psi=\Theta(\text{composite factor bars})$, built from the normalized intertwiner $\Theta$ of [[thm-the-weightwise-quasi-r-intertwiner-exists-and-is-unique]], is well defined, semilinear, $U$- and bar-compatible, involutive and independent of all parenthesizations; all root-height sums are vectorwise finite.

This field assertion holds for arbitrary based pairs and does not imply integral action. Its integral and based assertion holds for exactly the admissible cases proved by the integral-action supplier [[lem-quasi-r-divided-power-integrality-on-based-lattices]]: highest-first or first $C_{\mathrm{high}}$ with arbitrary based second; arbitrary based first with lowest or $C_{\mathrm{low}}$ second under finite action; all finite highest products and exact based subquotients and direct sums of their tensor constructions; ordered highest-prefix, based-middle, lowest-suffix products with explicit local support bounds; and arbitrary based pairs and products in finite Cartan type. For any other pair the same conclusion is conditional on an independently proved integral $\Theta$ action, not on field semisimplicity or lattice freeness.

In these cases: $\Psi$ preserves the divided-power integral tensor lattice; its action on raw tensor lower basis vectors is locally weight-transfer triangular with diagonal $1$; the actual tensor global vectors are its uniquely corrected bar-fixed lifts congruent to those raw tensor vectors modulo $q$, with corrections in $q\mathbb Z[q]$; they form a genuine $A$-basis and give the integral balanced tensor triple; the $q=0$ tensor lattice and crystal basis are supplied separately by the completed crystal tensor rule [[thm-crystal-basis-tensor-product-rule]], and the infinity chart is $\Psi(L_0^{\mathrm{tensor}})$, not an asserted bar containment in $L_0$, since semilinearity sends $q$ to $q^{-1}$. The raw tensor lower vectors are generally not bar fixed. Exact based integral and bar-compatible subquotient maps preserve the corrected global bases by balanced uniqueness. No assertion covers arbitrary two-sided-unbounded evaluation, semi-infinite limits, a universal-$R$ braiding, or general arbitrary-based integral action; the affine boundary in the supplier disproves the latter.

derivations.claim: **The module triple.** By [L1] and [L3], $V_A\cap L_0=\mathbb Z[q]v\oplus\mathbb Z[q]w$, whose quotient by $q(V_A\cap L_0)$ has $\mathbb Z$-basis the classes of $v$ and $w$; the same two vectors are exactly $E_{\mathbb Z}=\mathbb Zv\oplus\mathbb Zw$, so the integral globalization map is an isomorphism and the triple is balanced. The rational extension has basis the two classes over $\mathbb Q$. The lower global basis is $v,w$, congruent to the crystal classes.

**The string image.** The field string image is $FV=\mathbb Q(q)w$; the integral image ideal is $FV\cap V_A=Aw$, whose balanced part is $Aw\cap\psi(Aw)=\mathbb Zw$. The three spaces are genuinely different, as displayed.

**The tensor bar.** Applying [L4]: $E\otimes F$ kills $vv,vw,ww$ since $Ev=0$ and $Fw=0$, and sends $wv$ to $Ew\otimes Fv=v\otimes w=vw$; hence the four displayed formulas. $\Psi$ preserves total weight because $E\otimes F$ does, preserves the $A$-tensor lattice because $\Theta=1+(q-q^{-1})E\otimes F$ has $A$-coefficients, and is involutive because $(q-q^{-1})+\overline{(q-q^{-1})}=0$ and $(E\otimes F)^2=0$ on this module.

**The corrected tensor global basis.** The bar-fixed combinations are $vv,vw,ww$ and $wv+cvw$ with $c$ satisfying $c+q^{-1}(q-q^{-1})=c$, i.e. $c=q$; the transition matrix from the raw basis is unitriangular with off-diagonal $q$, so the corrected family $vv,vw,wv+qvw,ww$ is an $A$-basis congruent to the raw tensor basis modulo $q$, with zero crystal lattice the $A_0$-tensor lattice and balanced $\mathbb Z$-part its $\mathbb Z$-span; the raw $wv$ is not bar fixed.

**The nonbalanced mixed lattice.** For $L'=A_0(v+w)\oplus qA_0v$, an element $\alpha(v+w)+\beta v$ with $\alpha\in A_0$, $\beta\in qA_0$ lies in $V_A$ exactly when $\alpha\in\mathbb Z[q]$ and $\beta\in q\mathbb Z[q]$; lying in $\psi(L')=A_\infty(v+w)\oplus q^{-1}A_\infty v$ forces in addition $\alpha\in\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$ and $\beta\in q^{-1}\mathbb Z[q^{-1}]$ with Laurent degree bounds, so $\alpha\in\mathbb Z$ and $\beta=0$: the balanced part is exactly $\mathbb Z(v+w)$. The integral zero residue contains the independent class of $qv$, which is not in the image of $\mathbb Z(v+w)$, so $L'$ is not balanced; the bar-fixed vector $v+w$ alone does not repair this, and since $\tilde e(v+w)=v\notin L'$ the lattice is not crystal stable either.

**Conclusion.** Steps 1.1–1.2 compute the rank-one balanced triple and its string-image strata; steps 1.3–2.1 compute the exact quasi-$R$ action, the corrected tensor global basis and its lattice; step 2.2 exhibits the nonbalanced mixed lattice while distinguishing $v+w$ from the undefined class of $v$. All computations are finite, and the zero divisors $A/qA=0$ are never used for residues.
